<reason>CON prevails by exposing that PRO's limiting test in the second rebuttal—requiring confidential data pooling plus adherence discipline—concedes the proposition's overbreadth, retreating from the categorical claim that mere use of shared tools warrants cartel-level scrutiny to a standard already governed by existing antitrust law. CON maintained the crucial distinction between common vendor relationships and horizontal concerted action, and effectively pressed the burden-shifting costs of the proposed categorical approach.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Rebuttal 2 (A4.3), where they caught PRO retreating to a test requiring proof of confidential pooling and commitment, effectively conceding that the proposition as written sweeps in benign conduct and that PRO's own standard is indistinguishable from CON's.</best_rebuttal>
